newsitem.title: USA: NBA BASKETBALL-SPURS SELECT DUNCAN WITH TOP PICK IN DRAFT.
newsitem.headline: NBA BASKETBALL-SPURS SELECT DUNCAN WITH TOP PICK IN DRAFT.

text.p: The San Antonio Spurs surprised no one and selected centre Tim Duncan with the first pick in the 1997 draft Wednesday.
Ten years after the Spurs selected David Robinson with the top pick, they grabbed Duncan to play alongside him in a "Twin Towers" frontcourt.

The 6-10 (2.08 metres) Duncan has been regarded as the best player in college the last three years. He averaged 20.8 points and a nation-leading 14.7 rebounds per game last season at Wake Forest and was the consensus college player of the year.
But after his selection, the intrigue began.
With the second pick, the Philadelphia 76ers chose Utah forward Keith Van Horn -- but various unconfirmed reports said he was headed to the New Jersey Nets as part of an eight-player trade.

According to the reports, the 76ers would receive the seventh and 21st picks, guard Jim Jackson and centre Eric Montross from the Nets, who would receive forward Don MacLean, guard Lucious Harris and a player to be named, likely centre Michael Cage.

Van Horn has said he did not want to play for the 76ers. He is a three-time Western Athletic Conference Player of the Year who averaged 22 points and 9.5 rebounds per game with the ability to score both inside and outside.
With the third pick Rick Pitino, in his first selection as coach and president of the Boston Celtics, tabbed Colorado guard Chauncey Billups.

The Celtics were also embroiled in plenty of intrigue -- the voiding of a trade after Dino Radja refused to report for a medical examination by the 76ers, and apparently fruitless talks, confirmed by Pitino, about a possible trade for the NBA champion Chicago Bulls' star swingman Scottie Pippen.
The Vancouver Grizzlies chose Bowling Green point guard Antonio Daniels with the fourth pick, making him the second straight point guard selected.
The Denver Nuggets selected versatile forward-centre Tony Battie, who left Texas Tech a year early, with the fifth overall pick.
Forward Ron Mercer joined his former coach and teammate with the Boston Celtics, who made the Kentucky forward their second first-round draft choice and the sixth overall.

Mercer, who left Kentucky after his sophomore season, is reunited with coach Pitino and forward Antoine Walker, who was Boston's first-round pick in 1996 after teaming with Mercer to lead the Wildcats to the NCAA championship.
New Jersey, reportedly selecting for the 76ers as part of an eight-player trade, chose Villanova forward Tim Thomas with the seventh pick.
The Golden State Warriors, looking for defensive help, selected shot-blocker Adonal Foyle with the eighth pick. He left Colgate after his junior year.
The Toronto Raptors opted for youth with the ninth pick, selecting forward Tracy McGrady from Mount Zion Christian Academy High School in Durham, North Carolina.
The Milwaukee Bucks chose burly Cincinnati forward Danny Fortson with the 10th pick -- perhaps to be traded to another team.
